Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We loved the live batching/caching walkthrough and your examples around KV cache reuse for chat flows. A few things procurement and engineering asked me to clarify before we put together a procurement request: 

- Commercial: how do you structure short pilots for Optimize (credits vs time-limited discounts)? We want a simple path that lets us validate savings without a long commit.
- Savings ladder: do you offer a stepped credit/discount once we hit certain token thresholds during pilot -> production?
- Technical asks from infra team: recommended quantization (int8 vs int4) trade-offs for our clinical summarization pipeline, and whether the batcher can be pinned to lower-latency modes for interactive flows.
- SLA: any runtime guarantees for pilot customers? We need baseline latency numbers and an escalation path for production readiness.

I've attached a short RFP-style doc and the procurement contact is CC'd (procurement@stabilityhealth.com). Can you send a short commercial offer + a one-page tech recommendation by EOD Thursday?

Hi Elaine —

Really appreciate the clear list. High level response below; attaching a short SOW and a concise tech note with quantization + batching knobs (optimizer_quants_recs.xlsx). I'll keep the commercial section short so procurement has something to review quickly.

Commercial (pilot-first approach):
- Pilot structure: 4-week pilot with a credit pool (pre-purchased credits) plus a trial allowance. Typical pilot: $15k credit pool + $5k trial allowance that we won't bill unless you exceed trial usage. Credits are consumed against per-token consumption in the Optimize toolkit (includes batching, caching benefits).
- Savings ladder (produce-to-commit): If you convert to a production commit within 60 days post-pilot, we apply a retroactive credit equal to 20% of pilot credits back onto the first 3 months of committed usage. For larger commit bands (>= $150k/mo), ladder increases up to 30% retro credit and deeper per-token tiers.
- Flex path: no long-term lock required to try technical optimizations; commit only when you see metric improvements (latency / unit cost).

Technical recommendations (summary, see attached):
- Quantization: For clinical summarization with strict quality needs, start with dynamic INT8 quantization (best cost/quality balance). Run A/B evals against FP16 on a representative prompt set — INT4 is aggressive: good for batch-throughput workloads but likely to introduce tail-case token errors for rare medical tokens. We can provide a small eval harness during pilot.
- Batching/caching: enable prefix KV caching for recurring patient-summary contexts and use adaptive batching: keep interactive routes pinned to a low-latency lane (batch size 1-4, max wait 10ms) and throughput routes (export jobs) to high-batch lanes.
- Fallbacks: we recommend a two-variant route — quantized variant for high-throughput requests and a FP16/FP32 fallback for safety-critical responses. Smart routing in the runtime will failover if quality/regression alerts trigger.

Runtime guarantees for pilot: we can commit to a best-effort latency SLO (p50/p95 targets) in hosted pilot; production SLAs are available on Dedicated. For pilot, we provide: p50 30–60ms (token-produce), p95 250ms for interactive routes (depends on model and sequence length). Full latency matrix attached (latency_sla_matrix.csv).

Next steps I propose:
1) I send the attached 1-page SOW and the recommended pilot config (attached).
2) If procurement is happy, we sign a short pilot SOW and set up a tech kickoff (1 hour) with our inference engineers.
3) We run 2 weeks of data collection + 2 weeks of tuning/validation — at the end you'll have a clear delta report (cost per 1k tokens, latency distribution, quality regression pass rate).

I can iterate the commercial numbers if procurement needs a different credit structure.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the attachments and a proposed SOW id.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Lead, Optimize
Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We can accept the $10k credit pool on condition of a 6-week exclusive evaluation window and a short MSA addendum that covers pilot mechanics (retro credit terms, data handling). Summary of the updates below: 

- Pilot: $10k credits + $5k trial allowance (trial allowance kicked in only if you elect to go beyond the included test volume). 6-week exclusive window.
- Retro credit: contractual — if you sign a production commit within 60 days of pilot close, we will apply a credit equal to 20% of pilot credits across the first billing cycle as line-item credit. We'll include the exact language in the DocuSign SOW.
- Rollback/quality gates: SOW will include a QA acceptance test (representative prompt set). If >2% of sampled summaries fail the agreed QA, we will 1) pause quantized variant routing, 2) run an immediate triage and 3) apply remediation services (up to 8 engineering hours) included in the pilot.
- TCO sketch: attached one-pager that models three scenarios (FP baseline, INT8+cache, INT4 aggressive) with expected unit costs and latency bands. INT8 shows ~2.2x cost savings on unit token economics with similar quality; INT4 shows 3.5x but with higher risk.

I'll push the SOW to DocuSign after you confirm the $10k + 6-week window. If procurement wants, we can also convert the trial allowance into different billing treatment (capture as refundable credit on signature).

Proposed next step: procurement confirms and we send DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
—Mateo
